Dubai Real Estate AIPOC

Documentation

This is a proof of concept, not the full product. This page is the honest map of what's real, what's partial, and what's simulated — so a demo of this never overclaims what a customer would actually get today.

What's real vs. simulated

Text chat → AI pipeline

Real

Runs through the real LangGraph agent graph (scoring → qualifier → research → conversation → handoff), with a deterministic fallback if GROQ_API_KEY isn't set.

Voice chat → AI pipeline

Real

Fixed in this POC: speech is transcribed, then routed through the SAME agent pipeline as text (previously it echoed a canned line instead).

Property matching

Real

Fixed in this POC: scores leads against whatever inventory has actually been imported for this deployment, falling back to demo listings only when none exist yet (previously it always used 3 hardcoded demo units).

Multi-source property ingestion

Real

CSV upload, JSON/CRM import, manual URL import, approved feeds, and RapidAPI all write to the same properties table.

Property Finder live scraping

Partial

Works today. Bayut and Dubizzle scraping are deferred by default (both are anti-bot protected) — see the Configure pipeline step.

Workspace multi-tenancy

Simulated

The Configure wizard creates and saves a real workspace record. Leads/properties are NOT yet scoped by workspace — every workspace currently shares one inventory and lead pool.

WhatsApp sending

Simulated

The Channels step stores a WhatsApp number in the workspace config. No message actually sends — that integration doesn't exist yet.

Broker dashboard numbers

Simulated

Stat cards and pipeline board still render fixed mock data, not live queries.

Architecture at a glance

Lead sources

Chat widget, voice, WhatsApp (config only)

LangGraph agent pipeline

Scoring → Qualifier → Research → Conversation → Handoff/Nurture

Property inventory

CSV / CRM / approved feed / RapidAPI / Property Finder → one table

Workspace config

Team, data sources, channels — set via /configure

Supabase (or in-memory mock)

Leads, properties, brokers, conversations, workspaces

How Configure maps to the backend

POST /api/v1/workspace/ creates a workspace record from the wizard's team + data source + channel state.

Toggling a data source calls POST /api/v1/workspace/data-sources/{source}/test (for feed/API sources) or the real /api/v1/properties/import/csv endpoint (for CSV/CRM — actually imports rows, not a stub).

"Launch" calls POST /api/v1/workspace/{id}/launch, flipping status from draft to live.

Roadmap to a real product

  1. 1.Add workspace-scoping to leads, properties, and conversations (the biggest gap between this POC and a real multi-broker product).
  2. 2.Wire the dashboard to live data instead of mock arrays.
  3. 3.Real WhatsApp Business API send/receive per workspace number.
  4. 4.Authentication + billing so workspaces map to paying customers.
  5. 5.Automated tests around the agent graph and ingestion pipeline before onboarding real customer data.
